description:
## Goal
Prove exact recursive publication membership and canonical per-product group identity across process hash seeds on the retained reactive graph, without changing semantic pull behavior or restoring private cones.

## Current evidence and construction order
At HEAD 54f0162e3, fz-kdt.4 and fz-kdt.58 are complete. The existing six-subprocess target observation bundle compares the full canonical causal multiset with zero exclusions, including exact publisher/member publication edges and search work. Historical eager-cone implementation and oracle switches in the separate fz-wt-tfn2 worktree are obsolete evidence, not a patch to transplant.

The pre-change proof gap was in causal replay: ProductSettlement.group was emitted but discarded by CausalReport. The implementation retains those already-emitted settlement memberships in the report and canonicalizes their partitions without changing compiler execution. Equal counts and publisher/member multisets therefore do not prove equal publication partitions. ProductMemo allocates group IDs monotonically within its retained session; raw numbers identify one publication only within that session, not across builds.

## Strategy and TDD signal
Add a minimal public-event replay RED showing that identical product counts with a changed group partition compare equal incorrectly. Retain session-scoped raw group handles only as reporting joins; canonicalize actual group member multisets through the existing product identity authority at the report boundary. Group/session renumbering and nested-session group-number reuse must compare equal; a split or merged group must differ. No compiler member store, scheduler ordering, type display authority, or extra fixture compilation is justified.

## Acceptance
- Exact successful recursive publication membership and canonical per-product group membership are reproducible across independent process hash seeds.
- Existing target subprocess observations compare every canonical causal dimension with no exclusions and require non-vacuous group membership.
- Search counts and traversal remain those established by fz-tfn.25; no duplicate traversal or telemetry.
- Product values, settlements, backend artifacts, and runtime output retain fidelity. Proven-unused reductions are permitted only with causal proof per epic acceptance.
- The causal oracle detects changed partitions while ignoring incidental numeric group/session allocation order, preserving member multiplicity and repeated publications.
- Remove stale cutover documentation and transition-only paths. Do not modify the unrelated historical worktree.
- Run focused recursive-product/replay tests, target cross-process observations, full library, single-threaded fixture matrix, formatting and warnings-denied checks; fresh ticket-scoped cold review before commit.

## Non-goals
No private cone, snapshot replay, fixpoint pass, raw interner ordering or display-string semantic authority. Production changes require evidence from the strengthened oracle, not historical code.

## Completed implementation and verification (2026-09-05)
Initial RED: canonical_recursive_groups_preserve_partitions_not_session_local_numbers failed its assert_ne because paired and split publications produced identical reports. GREEN: the two permanent replay tests distinguish split/merged partitions, equal-cardinality AB/CD versus AC/BD, and singleton versus ordinary settlements; preserve equivalent raw member multiplicity and repeated publications across retained-session reactivation; and ignore session/group renumbering including nested-session group-number reuse.

ProductMemo already allocates one fresh group handle per successful group publication and retains its counter across session activations. Replay joins (session, group) only within the input trace. Canonical comparison uses the existing canonical product dictionary and sorted member vectors, never display types or raw numeric group/session order. No compiler scheduler, traversal, product allocation, or telemetry emission changed. The historical separate worktree was inspected read-only and not transplanted; the obsolete future-cutover documentation sentence is deleted. No construction switch or temporary fixture was introduced.

Final reviewed diff SHA-256: 5bf30548704563fdfa7826c047bdeee35009cc97fb1addb7863ea7cc23692ab5 (five files). Fresh ticket-scoped cold review by cold_tfn2 approved with no findings, contingent on the now-completed gates.

Final gates:
- cargo test --lib recursive_group -- --nocapture: 7 passed.
- cargo test --test fz2_cli target_fixture_public_causal_and_backend_observations_are_reproducible -- --nocapture: passed, six independent compiler processes over the three target fixtures; exact canonical group partitions, all causal dimensions, backend bytes, and runtime output agree, with nonempty successful groups and settlement/publication member totals cross-checked.
- cargo test --lib --quiet on final source: 1850 passed, 0 failed, 6 existing ignored.
- cargo test --test fz2_cli on final source: 30 passed, including the strengthened six-process oracle and interp/run/build boundaries.
- cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1: 531 passed, 0 failed (existing kind:test build deferrals remain unchanged).
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo check --workspace, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check: passed.
- cargo test --doc: passed, one existing ignored doctest.

Uncommitted handoff for root-owned commit/close and CI-gated push; unrelated untracked measurements remain preserved and excluded.

comments.text: TDD implementation ready for cold review (uncommitted). Red: focused five-node pending graph failed on legacy early-exit reach work with left=1/right=5. Design deletes the separate reachability gate and repeated per-candidate SCC walks; one Tarjan traversal includes the prospective current->dependency edge, so it simultaneously detects the cycle and returns its members. Across 32 fresh RandomState memos the report is exact: candidate_scans=5, reached_candidates=2, dependency_reach_visits=5; a naive exhaustive-per-candidate rewrite would cost 41 SCC visits plus a separate gate. Checks: pull tests 31/31; full lib 1587 passed/5 ignored; target fixture interp/run/build 9/9; fz2_cli causal cross-process pass; clippy all-targets -D warnings pass; git diff --check pass. fz-kdt.5 must retain its JSONL/causal wiring and rerun its three-fixture cross-process acceptance after applying this structural diff.

Post-fz-kdt.47 evidence: RuntimeDemand formula values, requested products, settled product sets, search-shape totals, and backend artifacts are stable across processes, but the current eager cone/product interaction closes different exact pending SCC member sets (union-typed versus narrower CallableConstruction activations). This is not a Ty alias defect and cannot be repaired by choosing a canonical resolver or folding activation identity. Reactive per-executable RuntimeDemand in fz-kdt.4 must remove the schedule-dependent pending graph before this ticket can require exact stable group membership. The raw causal ledger and focused red subprocess oracle are preserved.

Authorized DAG split: fz-tfn.25 now owns current-graph recursive-search work determinism. This ticket retains exact recursive publication membership only, after fz-kdt.4 removes eager RuntimeDemand cone scheduling.

title: Make recursive-group publication membership reproducible after RuntimeDemand cutover
